data.title: AI | Natalia Kniazhevich: Wall Street's AI Concerns Persist After Anthropic's Record IPO
data.description:
Anthropic’s record IPO failed to reverse deteriorating market sentiment as investors contended with Nvidia turmoil, concerns about AI spending and selling by systematic funds, according to Bloomberg. Bloomberg US equities reporter Natalia Kniazhevich discussed the market backdrop on Bloomberg This Weekend.

Goldman Sachs’ Panic Index reached 9 out of 10. Kniazhevich also discussed heavy positioning, weak liquidity and a potential wave of new stock issuance.

data.title: Retirees Face Dec. 31 RMD Deadline, With Penalties Up to 25%
data.description: According to CNBC, retirees who miss the Dec. 31 deadline for required minimum distributions (RMDs) may owe an IRS excise tax of up to 25% of the amount they should have withdrawn. Most retirees must begin taking RMDs from pretax accounts at age 73; the first withdrawal is due by April 1 of the following year, while later annual withdrawals are due by Dec. 31. Investors who correct a missed RMD within two years and file Form 5329 may reduce the penalty to 10%. A Vanguard analysis found that 7% of its investors at RMD age missed their annual withdrawal in 2025, compared with 6.7% in 2024.

data.title: Canton Approves CC Burn Mechanism for Mainnet, First Phase Planned for Q1 2027
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Canton has approved a plan to extend the CC token-burning mechanism to its mainnet. The institutional blockchain network plans to use token burns instead of its existing licensing-fee model, with burns carried out on dedicated synchronizers. The rollout will be phased, with the first phase tentatively scheduled to begin in the first quarter of 2027.

data.title: CryptoUK Urges FCA to Clarify DeFi Development Is Not Automatically a Regulated Activity
data.description:
CryptoUK has called on the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) to clarify that developing and governing decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols should not, by itself, be treated as a regulated activity. According to Odaily, in its response to the FCA’s consultation paper CP26/36, the association said software development, maintenance, security work and participation in decentralized governance should not constitute regulated activities, consistent with the FCA’s approach of identifying “clear controllers” in DeFi.

CryptoUK broadly supports the FCA’s draft guidance but said some provisions exceed the scope of legislation, including using the location of protocol development and governance as a basis for establishing a UK connection and imposing requirements on payment and own-account trading exemptions. The association also urged the FCA to publish a public list of stablecoins that comply with the UK regulatory framework and clarify the distinction between stablecoins and electronic money.

data.title: Jim Cramer Put Money to Work During Wall Street’s Worst Week in Over a Year
data.description: According to CNBC, Jim Cramer’s Charitable Trust bought shares of Advanced Micro Devices, FedEx Freight, Meta Platforms, Constellation Brands and Bank of New York during Wall Street’s worst week in more than a year. The S&P 500 fell 8.6% for the week, while the Nasdaq dropped 10%. The trust also completed a planned swap, selling Intel at an approximately 50% loss to start a position in AMD, and trimmed Apple after its 31% rally this year. It upgraded Meta to a buy-equivalent 1 rating after adding to the position.

data.title: Aave V4 Deposits Rise to $1.51 Billion as Loans Reach $595.5 Million
data.description: Aave V4 market deposits rose to about $1.51 billion, while loans increased to about $595.5 million. According to Odaily, citing Sentora data, deposits grew from about $496.3 million on August 22 to about $1.51 billion on November 19, roughly tripling; loans rose from about $174 million to about $595.5 million, or around 3.42 times. Loans as a share of deposits increased from 35.1% to 39.4%. From November 5 to 19, loans rose 16.3% and deposits increased 13.5%. The balance changes do not show whether borrowers migrated from V3, were new to Aave, or were affected by token price fluctuations.

data.title: XRP Could Post Its Worst Month in Recent History as Losses Top 28%
data.description:
XRP fell below $0.90 for the first time in nearly two years, trading near $0.89 after dropping more than 6% in 24 hours. November losses have topped 28%, putting the token on course for one of its worst months in recent history, according to BeInCrypto. If the decline continues through month-end, November could become XRP’s worst month of the year and surpass the 23.6% drop recorded in 2019. The token is more than 75% below its record high near $3.65 from July 2025.

XRP’s $0.90 support, which had held on a sustained basis since November 2024, gave way amid a broader crypto selloff. Bitcoin fell below $56,000, while U.S. stocks sold off on weakness in technology and AI shares; crypto liquidations topped $1 billion in recent sessions. The next support for XRP is near $0.80, with a more bearish scenario pointing to $0.64-$0.70. Spot XRP ETFs saw about $30.8 million in net outflows in November, putting them on track for their worst month since launching in November 2025; March holds the record at roughly $31.2 million. Total net assets fell to about $990 million from $1.42 billion in October. The token is considered oversold, but bulls would need to reclaim $0.90, then $0.99-$1.00, to open a path toward $1.10; a broader rebound could take XRP to $1.30-$1.50.

data.title: Binance Market Update | Bitcoin Crashes Below $57K as $2.4B Gets Wiped Out. Traders Bet on a Bull Market That Never Came
data.description: Bitcoin fell below $57,000, its lowest since September 2024, as $2.4B in futures were liquidated in 24 hours, then rebounded to about $59,300. The Nasdaq fell more than 4% Friday, and Nvidia dropped 14% to a 52-week low, down about $2.7T from its October record. XRP hit 87 cents, and US spot XRP ETF assets slipped below $1B. Kobeissi Letter calls the AI rout a correction, not a popped bubble, while US stocks have lost $6T since October 6. Tap to see what analysts say comes next.Bitcoin Falls Below $57,000 to a Two-Year Low as $2.4 Billion in Liquidations Hit Bullish TradersBitcoin fell below $57,000, its lowest since September 2024, then rebounded to about $59,300, still down about 29% for the quarter. It set a new low in the bear market that began after the peak above $126,000 in October 2025 (about 55% above Friday's low, calculated). It broke below its June low of under $58,000, erasing the September recovery above the 50-week average that Galaxy and others read as a new uptrend. The Nasdaq fell more than 4% Friday to its lowest since April, and gold, copper and Asian stocks also fell. Analysts point to rising real yields as the key driver. Liquidations reached $2.40B per CoinGlass: bitcoin over $1B, ether $545M, and the largest single liquidation a $51.71M bitcoin long. CoinDesk said positioning was heavily tilted toward a bull market, with many traders not expecting a drop below $60,000.Tech Stocks Slide as AI Sentiment Cools, Nvidia Loses $2.7 Trillion in a Month and a HalfNvidia fell 14.01% on November 20 to a 52-week low, with its market cap near $3T, fourth among US stocks after Alphabet overtook it. It is down from a record of about $5.77T set October 6, a drop equal to Amazon's entire market cap. Anthropic gave back most of its debut gains on day two, closing down 8.50% after briefly nearing its $83 IPO price. Media attribute Nvidia's fall to weaker AI sentiment, the broader tech selloff and concerns about the company's accounting.Kobeissi Letter Calls AI Rout a Correction, Not a Popped BubbleUS stocks have lost an average of $225B a day for 31 straight sessions, $6T since the S&P 500's October 6 record. Kobeissi argues capex is the trigger: Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft capex hit a record $201.9B in Q3, up $36.9B. Earnings held up, with S&P 500 Q3 EPS up 31.9% year over year. It says the Democratic sweep ended the "Trump Put," that Anthropic's IPO drained liquidity (demand of $400B institutional and $100B retail, nearly eight times the $64.4B sought), and that Nvidia, down 40%, trades at 9x forward earnings. A November 19 short-seller report accused AMD of smuggling chips to China, which the letter calls far from substantiated. The VIX is up more than 100% from its October low. It stops short of calling a bottom, saying another 10% decline would still be a healthy correction.XRP Drops to Two-Year Low Near 87 Cents as Spot ETF Assets Fall Below $1 BillionXRP fell to about 87 cents Saturday, its lowest since November 2024, down about 9% over 24 hours and 11.5% over the week. The five US spot XRP ETFs hold about $990M in net assets against about $1.78B in cumulative inflows; the gap reflects falling market value. Ether dropped more than 10%, SOL more than 9% and Zcash 19%. About $18M of XRP futures were liquidated, roughly 94% longs, and funding turned negative. XRP's daily RSI is below 30, oversold, which can precede short-term rebounds but does not confirm a bottom.China-Related Stocks Mostly Fall on November 21; TSMC Drops 9.48%, Alibaba 2.68%The Nasdaq Golden Dragon China Index fell 3.37%. TSMC -9.48%, ASE Technology -13.84%, XPeng -13.86%, UMC -10.15%, Baidu -6.75%, Li Auto -7.56%, NIO -7.89%, Alibaba -2.68%. H World rose 0.14%.

data.title: Unloved Stocks Rally as AI Trade Loses Steam
data.description: According to CNBC, the Nasdaq Composite is down 2.7% in 2026 and has fallen 14% over the past month as the AI trade lost steam, while several out-of-favor non-AI stocks advanced. The Campbell's Company rose nearly 20% over the past month, even though only one of 23 analysts rates it a buy, FactSet data showed. BTIG chief market technician Jonathan Krinsky said low investor ownership and widespread lack of interest could set up the stock for a sharp move higher, with a potential trading-volume area near $30. Clorox also gained roughly 20% over the past month, despite analysts' average forecast for an 11% decline over the next 12 months. JetBlue Airways rose 14%; only one analyst rates the airline a buy, and it faces higher fuel costs. Boston Beer advanced nearly 13% after raising its full-year adjusted earnings guidance in October to $9 to $10.50 per share, above FactSet's $8.90 consensus estimate. Only 6.7% of analysts covering Boston Beer rate it a buy. Lululemon and Prudential Financial also appeared on the list of unpopular stocks that outperformed the broader market over the past month.

data.title: Anthropic's Record IPO Debut Coincides With Tech's Worst Week on Wall Street Since 2020
data.description: According to CNBC, Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO and secured an additional $26 billion from technology companies that bought shares at the offering price. The stock rose 17% in its Thursday debut, giving the company a $1.8 trillion market capitalization. The debut came as technology shares suffered their worst week since 2020: Nvidia fell 23%, its sharpest weekly decline in 18 years, and the Nasdaq dropped 10% over the past five trading days.

data.title: Tech Outages Drive Surge in Emergency-Prep Spending
data.description: According to CNBC, spending at brands specializing in emergency products rose about 400% from a year earlier between Nov. 12 and Nov. 17, when at least half a dozen major technology outages occurred in the U.S. Ready America’s e-commerce sales increased roughly fivefold in recent days, and the company asked suppliers to increase production. Mizuho expects Costco’s non-fuel sales growth in November to top 10% for the first time since 2022, as shoppers stock up on emergency supplies. The Global X Cybersecurity ETF (BUG) gained about 2.5% over the past two weeks, while the Nasdaq Composite fell into negative territory for 2026 on Friday.

data.title: Trump Rally Gains Fade as AI Investment Concerns Pressure U.S. Stocks and Crypto
data.description:
U.S. stocks and cryptocurrency markets sold off sharply this week amid concerns over AI investment and the fading of gains associated with U.S. President Donald Trump. According to Odaily, Bitcoin briefly fell below $56,000 for the first time since September 2024, erasing all gains since Trump won that year’s U.S. election. The total cryptocurrency market value has fallen about $2.3 trillion from its record high, with hundreds of billions of dollars flowing out in the past month alone.

U.S. stocks also came under pressure. The Nasdaq fell 5.3% on Friday, wiping out its gains for the year. The S&P 500 recorded its worst weekly performance since April 2025 and fell more than 10% from its October peak, entering correction territory.

Market analysts said the selloff began before Democrats regained control of the House and Senate and was driven mainly by concerns about large technology companies’ substantial AI investments. Since the S&P 500 reached a high on October 6, the estimated market value of U.S. stocks has declined by about $6 trillion. Analysts also said the Democratic victory may end the so-called “Trump Put”—the belief that Trump would step in to stabilize markets under pressure.

Technology analyst Dan Ives described the market environment as a “perfect storm,” citing investor concerns that a Democratic-controlled Congress may be less supportive of the AI industry and data center construction. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s high-profile departure, investigations involving the company and the possibility of further Federal Reserve rate hikes have also unsettled markets. The selloff is still viewed as a market correction, and Ives said his long-term view of AI had not changed.
